subject: redPanda
pitch:
Category: Animal.
Subject: red panda balancing on a mossy stone.
Style: Genshin Impact.
reasoning:
I'm planning a compact but detailed module for a red panda model in a resting pose on a mossy stone, using the toon kit's cel shading and anime eye decals, with realistic proportions scaled to a small animal.

Now I'm defining the joint hierarchy: hips as the root with a spine chain running from lower back to chest via catmull curves, then a neck and head joint positioned above the spine, calculating positions relative to the stone's top surface so the feet rest naturally at ground level.

For the head, I'm sketching the skull as a scaled sphere with a separate cream-colored muzzle and black nose, plus a lower jaw piece attached to its own joint for mouth movement. Eyes will be decal surfaces placed on the skull mesh, and I'm noting the red panda's characteristic dark tear-mark coloring around them.

Now I'm figuring out the ears as flattened spheres oriented outward with a cream inner disc, cheek ruffs as cream cone spikes attached to the head bone, and the body as a sweep along the spine chain with a radius function controlling thickness.

For color I'm using a cel-shaded fur edge effect with rust tones on the back and darker brown on the belly for countershading. I'm extending the spine path from the rump to the shoulders with specific coordinates and tapering the radius to shape the torso properly.

Adjusting spine endpoints so the body doesn't overlap too much with the neck and head, then placing the neck joint and head center so the proportions read naturally before moving on to leg placement at the shoulders.

Now I'm positioning the legs: shoulders and hips with specific offsets, feet targets based on stance height, and limb segment lengths that allow natural bending—elbows bending backward for front legs and knees bending forward for hind legs. I'm naming the joints and roles, setting parent relationships to the spine and hips, and defining sweep radii for the leg chains.

For paws, I'm using flattened spheres with small spheres added for toe bumps, roughly three per paw across all four legs. I'm keeping the pose neutral but with a wide stance for balance, and starting to curve the tail upward from the rump using a smooth spline path.

Continuing the tail, I'm tapering its radius toward the tip and painting it with alternating rust and darker red stripe bands along its length, using a cel-shaded stripe pattern wrapped around three named tail segments for the sweep.

For the stone, I'm considering options like a squashed icosahedron versus a lathed profile, settling on a chunky lathe shape with a flat top, defining the outline points to build a rounded bottom and flattened upper surface.

Since lathe options don't support scaling, I'll skip that and keep the stone round, attaching it to the hips joint since that's the nearest bone — it'll ride along with animation, which is acceptable. For moss, I'm scattering small tuft spikes on the upper surface where n.y>0.5, colored moss green, plus thinking about face markings like cream cheek paint applied via a position-based skull paint function.

For head details, I'm adding separate cream parts — a muzzle sphere, cheek ruffs, and brow dots above the eyes — plus a dark tear-line drape running from near the eye bottom down to the muzzle corner using a skin drape on a polyline, avoiding riskier floating geometry.

Now working out positions: eyes at ±38° azimuth with appropriate spacing, a cream muzzle sphere offset below the head center, a small dark nose sphere, and a cream lower jaw sphere positioned on the jaw bone.

I still need an explicit jaw joint between head and jaw, aiming forward so it can open and close, and I'll skip adding a separate mouth-interior detail to keep things simple. For the neck, I'm planning a short single-span sweep along a one-joint chain using a rust-toned coat color.

Now for the ears, I'm positioning them symmetrically off the head center, building each as a small flattened sphere oriented outward and upward with rust coloring, then layering a smaller cream-colored inner sphere offset slightly along the same direction to mimic the pale ear fringe seen on red pandas.

Beyond that, I'm adding small cream spheres above the eyes for the forehead brow spots, and then generating a short row of spike shapes along the cheek/forehead rim for the ruffed fur texture, spacing them with slight offsets in position and direction for a layered look.

For the body, I'm thinking about whether the chest should be a darker countershaded tone contrasting with the rust body, using a cel-shaded paint resolve. I'm also considering adding a small decorative touch in the Genshin style — maybe a ribbon or gold bell collar looped around the neck joint, built as a swept surface across the neck bone's position and axis.

Placing collar and bell...

For eyes I'll go with an amber iris around "#ffb43a" for that warm Genshin-like glint. Paws get flattened spheres positioned at each leg chain's tip joint, slightly offset and scaled thin to read as foot pads sitting near the ground plane.

I'm skipping claws and toe details for now to keep things simple, and setting up the core color palette with rust, cream, dark, moss, and stone tones for the whole model.

For the tail, I'm layering rust and darker rust stripes running along the tail's axis with some wobble for a natural look, then adding a cream-colored tip band near the end to finish the gradient transition.

I'm also wiring up the bone hierarchy—spine joints parented from the hips, hind legs attached at the hip position with two-segment limb chains computed from root to target positions, making sure the rump area stays covered by the spine bone.

For the front legs I'm setting up a similar limb chain with a forward-bending knee, and tagging left/right bones with suffixes since left corresponds to the positive X side. The hind legs get thicker sweep radii than the front for a sturdier look.

Now I'm building the tail as a short bone chain rooted inside the rump, then moving on to the stone's moss detailing—adding moss over the top and draping it along the edges, plus a patch underneath the panda—before writing the lathe geometry and paint function for the stone itself.

I'm defining the stone's cel-shaded paint rule so moss appears on upward-facing noisy patches and the rest alternates between two stone tones, then scattering small cone-shaped moss tufts across the stone's upward surfaces while avoiding strict exclusion near the panda's paws for simplicity.

I'm deciding to skip extra textures beyond the eyes given time constraints, and moving on to placing the eye decals with mirrored positioning on the surface.

Now I'm working out the whisker and tear-line details with draped polylines and thin swept tubes near the face surface, then adding flat cel-shaded colors to parts for a toon look.
